STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat plate (round). It has a rim band and a flat centre with no inner wall or shadow.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: the plate looks like a large round dinner plate, about 26-28 cm, but the photo is a bit angled and the plate sits close to the frame edges, so I take it as a standard round dinner plate.
b) Reference cue: the carrot slices are about 3-4 cm across. The chicken pieces are roughly 8-10 cm long. Across the plate, the food spans about 2.5-3 chicken-length widths, which points to roughly 25-27 cm.
Final width: 26 cm. Area = 0.785 x 26² ≈ 531 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items (estimated footprint share and thickness):
- Roasted eggplant and carrot cubes (top-left mound): ~18% of plate = 96 cm², mound about 2.5 cm average. Volume ≈ 240 ml x 0.6 (chopped vegetables) ≈ 145 g.
- Carrot slices (top, upper-middle): ~8% = 42 cm², ~1 cm thick. Volume ≈ 42 ml x 0.6 ≈ 25 g.
- Tofu cubes (lower-left): ~12% = 64 cm², ~2 cm average. Volume ≈ 128 ml x 1.0 ≈ 128 g.
- Beef or meat strips with leafy greens (lower-middle): ~10% = 53 cm², ~1.5 cm. Volume ≈ 80 ml; meat share ~60 g, greens ~20 g.
- Chicken breast or fish fillet (right side, two to three pieces): ~25% = 133 cm², ~2.5 cm. Volume ≈ 333 ml x 1.0 ≈ 300 g; fish/chicken share taken as 300 g.
- Fennel or herb garnish and leafy greens (scattered): ~5 g, negligible.
- Light oil or sauce on the vegetables: ~5 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no clear base layer under the toppings; the plate is essentially a single layer, so no extra items.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Eggplant and carrot (roasted with oil): ~90 kcal/100 g.
- Carrot, raw/cooked: ~35 kcal/100 g.
- Tofu, pan-fried: ~140 kcal/100 g.
- Beef strips: ~200 kcal/100 g.
- Leafy greens: ~25 kcal/100 g.
- Chicken or white fish, pan-cooked with coating: ~190 kcal/100 g.
- Oil: ~880 kcal/100 g.

Total weight ≈ 145 + 25 + 128 + 60 + 20 + 300 + 5 + 5 ≈ 690 g.
